scope: Fourth conservative local backfill for Belgian airbases with public airport/airfield history date evidence.

candidates.name: Beauvechain Air Base
candidates.source_notes: Airport history identifies Beauvechain/Le Culot as a Belgian Air Force military airfield established in 1936; the same page cites Belgian AIP as an airport source.
candidates.rationale: Exact overlay name match and active Belgian Air Force airbase; start year uses the documented military airfield establishment date.

candidates.name: Florennes Air Base
candidates.source_notes: Florennes airfield histories describe construction/use by the Luftwaffe in 1942 and continuing postwar Belgian military use; public airport records identify it as an operational Belgian Air Force base.
candidates.rationale: Exact overlay name match; 1942 is the more conservative documented air-base construction/use date rather than relying on broader airfield claims.

candidates.name: Jehonville Air Base
candidates.source_notes: Jehonville/Bertrix airbase history says it was constructed in 1958 for NATO dispersal and became operational on 29 August 1958; Forgotten Airfields corroborates its 1950s NATO reserve-airfield origin.
candidates.rationale: Exact overlay name match; start year follows the documented construction/operational date for the NATO reserve airfield.

candidates.name: Melsbroek Bel Air Base
candidates.source_notes: Aviation Safety Network airport profile lists Melsbroek Advanced Landing Ground B-58 opened in 1940; Wikidata also gives 1940 for Melsbroek Air Base.
candidates.rationale: Overlay name corresponds to Melsbroek Air Base/EBMB; start year follows public airport-history records.
